poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Bets on a hold climbed after the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs in September against 90,000 expected, and the Fed was seen skipping an October hike. Most Federal Reserve officials still expect another hike by year-end, and Collins called higher rates likely this year, which pushed the move later rather than to this meeting.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian and NATO forces clash directly before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with incidents on the alliance's border and with Ukraine talks.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The fortnight's news concerned the war in Ukraine and efforts to end it, not NATO: Washington hosted Ukraine and Europe in Miami without Russia, and Kyiv paused refinery strikes for two days under Trump's energy ceasefire, saying Russia ignored it. None of it set Russia against an alliance member, and none accounts for the price.

stocks:CVE.standing: A Calgary-based oil company and one of the largest producers in Canada's oil sands, with its own refineries in Canada and the United States. Its earnings turn on the discount heavy Canadian crude sells at against the US benchmark.
stocks:CVE.recent: Li Ka-shing's family sold a British grid for HK$110 billion and bought into Canadian oil sands, a swap that came after the share had already slid. Nothing in it accounts for the fall.

stocks:0001.HK.standing: A Hong Kong conglomerate built by Li Ka-shing, with ports, retail chains, telecoms networks and infrastructure across some 50 countries. Most of its earnings come from outside Hong Kong, so it trades on global trade and deal-making.
stocks:0001.HK.recent: Li Ka-shing's family sold a British grid for HK$110 billion, moving money out of regulated power networks. The sale was reported after the stretch the chart covers, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The one story about Tencent's own business was the retirement of its QClaw desktop agent, which shuts on 24 December. That came after the slide had already turned, and nothing in the input accounts for the share price.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: The trough came as Alibaba took the Pentagon to court, contesting its classification by the department and denying any link to the Chinese military. For a US-listed share, that designation reaches the holders themselves.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins the U.S. Senate seat from Texas in the November 2026 midterms. Texas has not elected a Democrat statewide since 1994, so the price tracks how competitive the race has become.
poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.recent: The fortnight's reporting on prediction markets concerned their legality: 39 states and 145 tribal nations urged the Supreme Court to take up the question. Nothing in it concerned the Texas race itself, and none of it accounts for the shift in this contract.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon's own news ran on several fronts: Amazon Leo built its 1,000th satellite and is weeks from a space Internet rollout, Alexa's leadership was reshuffled after a high-end tablet release, and Amazon may spend $7 billion on Decart, an AI startup Anthropic walked away from. None of it was tied to the share price.

stocks:EBAY.standing: An online marketplace where individuals and businesses sell new and used goods by auction or at a fixed price. It holds no stock itself and earns fees on each sale, so its revenue follows how much consumers spend through it.

stocks:AIR.PA.standing: Europe's largest aerospace company and one of the two builders of large passenger jets, with defence, helicopter and space arms. Its share moves on how many aircraft it delivers against a backlog that runs years ahead.
stocks:AIR.PA.recent: The fortnight's news on Airbus was defence and space work, not airliners: ESA picked Airbus and OHB to study a European-led space station, Spain chose the A321 for a new electronic intelligence aircraft, and the U740 Valkyrie drone flew at Mach 0.8. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: Brazil's first round, held alongside votes for governors and Congress, went to a runoff, and Bolsonaro's strong showing left Brazil's left on the ropes. That result moved money onto a mid-sized Bolsonaro win. Nothing reported since then explains the later swings within this margin band.

stocks:KTOS.standing: A San Diego defense contractor that builds jet-powered target drones and low-cost uncrewed combat aircraft, among them the XQ-58A Valkyrie. Its revenue depends on how far the Pentagon commits to cheap, expendable aircraft.
stocks:KTOS.recent: Airbus says its U740, the European variant of the XQ-58A Valkyrie, has flown at Mach 0.8 in Northern Europe. That is a step forward for the drone Kratos designed, and it does not account for the fall in the share.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile lifted the shares 4% in a day, while Verizon and AT&T fell 7% on the same news. Against that, Starlink still holds an Indian licence it cannot yet sell service under, and Elon Musk has turned the delay into a public fight with Ambani.

poly-us-x-yemen-ceasefire-continues-thro.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between the United States and Yemen's Houthis is still in force at its deadline. The Houthis sit beside Bab al-Mandeb, the strait Red Sea shipping between Europe and Asia passes.
poly-us-x-yemen-ceasefire-continues-thro.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport on consecutive days, killing at least 3 and grounding Lufthansa, Air India and Qatar Airways flights, while Yemen's government said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on a push toward Bab al-Mandeb. All of it pitted the Houthis against Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government; none of it named a US target.

stocks:1211.HK.standing: The Shenzhen carmaker that builds only battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles and makes its own batteries. Its price cuts set the pace of China's car market, and its exports draw tariffs abroad.

stocks:NOC.standing: A US defence contractor that builds the B-21 stealth bomber, the Sentinel nuclear missile, satellites and rocket motors. Most of its revenue comes from the US government, so its share follows the defence budget.
stocks:NOC.recent: Northrop's Talon Blue, a Collaborative Combat Aircraft, completed its first fully autonomous flight at Mojave on 3 October. Nothing else in the window was about the company's own business, and a first flight does not account for the fall in its share.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that pays out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. It moves on his standing against rivals inside the party, well before any primary vote.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before its deadline, by death, resignation or removal. Its price is what traders will pay for a change at the top of a nuclear state at war.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The fortnight's news from Russia was about the war around Putin, not his hold on office. Washington announced an energy truce that Kyiv answered with a two-day pause on refinery strikes, Ukrainian drones knocked out Yandex data centers, and talks in Miami went ahead without Russia. None of it bears on whether he leaves power.

stocks:9984.T.standing: A Tokyo-listed holding company run by founder Masayoshi Son that owns most of chip designer Arm and backs technology firms through its Vision Funds. Its share moves with what investors will pay for AI.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and the world's biggest maker of memory chips, alongside phones and displays. It is the heaviest weight in Seoul's benchmark index, so its share moves the whole market.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung forecast a record 107.4 trillion won profit, a 780% jump in quarterly operating profit on the AI boom, and the share fell anyway. The selloff in Seoul turned on questions over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and with SK Hynix it dragged South Korea's benchmark index down 5.5%.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: South Korea's second-largest chipmaker, making the DRAM and NAND memory inside servers, phones and PCs. It is a leading supplier of the high-bandwidth memory stacked beside AI processors, so its share follows data-centre spending.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% in a single session. The selling turned on two pressures on the memory makers: AI spending, the demand behind their most profitable chips, and competition from Chinese memory rivals.

stocks:BHP.standing: An Australian miner, one of the world's largest, based in Melbourne. It digs iron ore in Western Australia and copper in Chile, so its share moves with Chinese steel demand and the copper price.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.

poly-will-indiana-enact-a-data-center-mo.standing: A contract that pays out if Indiana enacts a statewide pause on new data centers before 2027. The state draws large server-farm projects, and local fights over power bills and water make it a test of how far the backlash reaches.

poly-will-louisiana-enact-a-data-center-.standing: A contract that pays out if Louisiana bans new data centers before its deadline. The state hosts one of the largest AI campuses being built in the US, so it prices the local backlash over power and water.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority of the US House of Representatives in the midterms. The price is what traders pay for that outcome; the House majority controls spending bills and investigations.

stocks:7974.T.standing: The Kyoto company that makes the Switch consoles and the Mario and Zelda games that sell them. It earns from its own hardware and its own software together, so its profits rise and fall with each console's life cycle.

stocks:UBI.PA.standing: The French publisher behind Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six, listed in Paris. Its fortunes ride on a few big releases a year, so a delay or a weak launch moves the share more than the wider games market does.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its December meeting. The price is what traders pay for a hold over a hike or a cut, and it moves with each jobs and inflation report.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end, and Collins said higher rates were likely this year to tame prices. A stalled jobs report, 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, had the Fed seen skipping its October hike rather than dropping the year-end one. That leaves December as the meeting in play.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for much of the Gulf's oil and gas exports, is back to normal by December 31. Its price is what traders will stake on that outcome.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Iran and Oman agreed coordinates for safe lanes, then the shooting resumed: Iran's Guards claimed mine strikes on supertankers, a US jet disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica for running the blockade, and Iran said Washington met only some of its seven conditions for reopening Hormuz. Six ships were hit in a single day soon after.

wiki-openai.standing: How many people read the English Wikipedia article on OpenAI each day, the San Francisco lab behind ChatGPT. It jumps when the company ships a model, loses a senior figure or lands in a dispute.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI released more than 350 mathematical findings in one day, after researchers in Cambridge rushed out a 95-page paper ahead of an OpenAI proof. In the same fortnight the Wikimedia Foundation said OpenAI agents crawled millions of its pages, and safety-report lead David Robinson quit after 3½ years.

stocks:BAC.standing: The second-largest US bank by assets, listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Its share price tracks US interest rates, consumer credit and deposit flows across tens of millions of American accounts.
stocks:BAC.recent: The US Treasury fined the bank more than $1.21bn for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, the third-largest penalty in the department's history, after it reported $5 billion in suspicious transactions late. The fine landed on 2026-10-14, after the last close shown, so it does not account for the slide before it.

stocks:SHEL.standing: One of the world's largest oil and gas companies, headquartered in London, and the biggest trader of liquefied natural gas. Its shares move with crude and gas prices and with the cash it returns to shareholders.
stocks:SHEL.recent: Shell agreed to sell Shell Nigeria Gas, which pipes gas to factories and power users in Nigeria, to Vaaris Energy, and Declassified UK reported that BP and Shell have signed agreements in Venezuela since January. Neither explains the share price: the Nigerian sale was announced after its latest close.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Houthis claimed a strike on an oil facility near Riyadh as smoke rose near Aramco there. Days later Aramco's CEO said almost 3 billion barrels of supply had been lost and that replenishing crude and fuel could take two years. Saudi Arabia then unexpectedly cut oil prices to Asia.

poly-will-google-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Google holds the top spot on a public AI-model leaderboard at the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay on Google leading OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs.

poly-will-bernadette-wilson-win-the-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bernadette Wilson wins Alaska's 2026 race for governor, an open seat because Mike Dunleavy is term-limited. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Naftali Bennett, who led the 2021–22 coalition that briefly unseated Benjamin Netanyahu, becomes Israel's next prime minister. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news concerned Bennett or an Israeli election. It was dominated by the cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, Israel ordering 20 British diplomats out, and a CIA report warning Israel risks civil war, and none of it accounts for the price.

stocks:COIN.standing: The largest US cryptocurrency exchange, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from trading fees and the interest on USDC stablecoin reserves, so its shares rise and fall with crypto prices and trading volume.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: A large SpaceX purchase of Nvidia hardware was the one piece of company news inside the window, and nothing in the reporting ties it to the price. Just after, an IDC report put Nvidia at 34% of China's data-centre AI accelerator market against Huawei's 28%, with its China shipments down 44% as US export controls built demand for domestic chips.
